content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working with a sensor connected to a [product_name]. My program already converts the sensor's 0-10V signal into a range from 0 to 1000 (for example, 5V becomes 500). Now, I need to further convert this value so that it shows the actual pressure for display on the HMI. For reference, 500 (5V) should be 0 mbar, 400 (4V) should be -200 mbar, and 300 (3V) should be -400 mbar, etc. The bolded value must be visible on the HMI. Values above 0 mbar aren't needed, since the sensor only measures diastolic pressure. Any advice?
Hi [user_name], Please note that English or German are the forum's languages. (This is a translation via Google Translate.) Best regards, [user_name]
Sorry, I didn't quite get your program setup. Could you explain how you intend to link these values to an I/O field?
I'm also not clear on what you mean by the I/O field specifically ... could you elaborate?

By I/O field I mean the display field in [product_name] engineering platform (version_no removed for privacy). I want to link these converted values to that display field, so the pressure can be visualized on the HMI screen instead of just on the [product_name] device itself.
You'll need to use Parameter VM Mapping. Please refer to the attached video for guidance.

Hello, How can I configure the I/O field to display negative values? I've read a few topics mentioning settings like S999.9, but I'm unsure about the location or if there are other steps required. Any suggestions?
Which data type have you chosen for the I/O field? If it's set to Word, that's incorrect; it needs to be set as INT instead.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are discussing methods to convert and display analog signal values from a sensor as pressure readings using a [product_name] device. Challenges center around mapping voltage to pressure, handling negative values on the HMI, and configuring I/O fields correctly (including datatype selection and proper linkage in the software environment). The conversation highlights confusion about technical details like I/O field setup and data mapping.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to reliably convert sensor voltages into accurate pressure readings (with support for negative values) and make sure these readings are correctly displayed on the HMI, with proper software-hardware integration and display configuration.
